title: The Claw Hero's Younger Brother
text: “Well then, extermination complete, I say.”
Wolf, whose attacks had been cutting through empty air, started flapping his jaw open and shut in dissatisfaction, opening his mouth at me over and over, but I paid it no mind.
“Was it really necessary to jump in from the side like that?”
“Normally you’d let him have that one, wouldn’t you?”
“Eeehhh…… Motoyasu-kun?”
“I mean…… I was watching from a distance, but in the middle of the fight, while everyone’s attention was on Wolf and his opponent, that guy suddenly blew the heads off three of them out of nowhere.”

The felled Dragon Emperor and griffin were bulging and shifting back into their monster forms. Being in a back alley, they swelled up large enough to block the passage, and on top of that things had gotten thoroughly bloody. Couldn’t be helped, so I used one of my spears to hack up Takt’s Dragon Emperor, the griffin, and the fox corpse, rolling them aside to clear the way.

The Takts, twitching and convulsing as their surrounding pigs and monsters were disposed of, kept their eyes fixed steadily in a glare at me. Ah, I’d gone ahead and properly cauterized Takt’s one arm that was dripping blood everywhere with fire magic to stop the bleeding.

Can’t have him dying just yet, after all — wouldn’t be able to make him suffer properly then. Takt, though numbed, was glaring at me like I’d killed his own parent, but I paid it no mind. Suffer more, I say. What an unsightly little three-colored dango of Takts.
“It looks like you basically wiped them all out, but…… what exactly were these guys?”
“This one’s——”
Wolf tried to explain to Father, but I’ll handle that, I say.

“This is Takt. On the surface he’s the Whip Seven Star Hero affiliated with Faubrey, but behind that facade he’s steeped himself in all manner of evil deeds — garbage of this world, I say. What’s more, he’s a reincarnator with memories of a past life, apparently one of the Wave’s vanguard.”
Takt, moth to the flame. Well then, I’ve gone and taken him alive. From here on, I’m going to make you suffer to your heart’s content. If you think you’ll get to die easy, you’re sorely mistaken.
“In the future, he goes on to kill numerous Seven Star Heroes and steal their Seven Star Weapons for himself, but he loses to us in the end, I say.”
“Holding multiple Seven Star Weapons at once? That shouldn’t even be possible.”
“Making the impossible possible is exactly what Takt does — he’s the Wave’s vanguard, a reincarnator, I say.”
“Something about being a ‘reincarnator,’ one of the Wave’s vanguard, apparently……”
Rabbit Guy was saying it couldn’t be true, but it was fact, I say.

“This one, across countless loops, has had the audacity to crack open Filolial-sama eggs by the dozens. So the punishment for that must be carried out in every single loop, no matter what, I saaaaaay!!!”

Which is precisely why, Wolf, I cannot simply overlook you finishing off Takt, understand? I’ll show you plenty of him suffering, so just be patient, all right? Trying to convey that unspoken message, I flashed a smile, and Wolf flinched, shuddering as if pulling back, tail tucking between his legs.
“Kyain!?”
From there he somehow circled around behind Father as if to hide. His body had gotten too big to fully hide behind him, though.
“There are parts I can’t quite follow since you’re skipping over so much, but did that idiot over there do something in some loop to earn a grudge like that?”

Father muttered with a sigh at the sight of it all. That’s right. Takt is the name of a creature who must, in every single loop, be tortured to the point of regretting he was ever born into this world.
“Elmelo-san has done that person a great kindness and is remembered fondly for it, but I really don’t want it to be the opposite for that guy. I should be careful not to be remembered badly myself.”
“Using it skillfully to our advantage is also an option, don’t you think? Wouldn’t the version of yourself in whatever world that guy ends up in next want to meet Shield Hero-sama again?”
“I see, that’s one way of thinking about it too, Shion. You really are a schemer.”

Rabbit Guy and the others were saying something or other, but go ahead and try it if you can, I say. Elephant is a good Elephant, I say. If Panda won’t do, perhaps I should rely on Elephant instead? With Father, it just might work out. After all, Father’s love isn’t about outward appearances.
“Anyway…… the fact that you’ve become able to speak means you’ve regained yourself, your memories? It sounds like you went through some pretty rough memories and human experimentation.”

Father turned to Wolf and asked. It seemed he’d been reduced to a beast through human experimentation that had messed with his head. Wolf came back to himself and gave a stiff, rugged sort of nod. Well, since I’d gone and stolen his right to beat Takt to a pulp, perhaps I should throw him a bit of a lifeline?
“Father prefers those who don’t speak human language from the start, I say. Speaking lowers one’s evaluation somewhat.”
“Motoyasu-kun, what are you even saying?”

Well, Chick said so herself, I say. Apparently the other male Rival also avoided learning human speech for that very reason. Rival went ahead and started speaking properly, though, and because of that, people kept their distance from it.
It seemed Wolf had decided to stop speaking in human words.
“You don’t need to pay any attention to what Motoyasu-kun says!”
Father gave a light cough and looked back at Wolf again.
“So, what settled into your hand there is…… the Claw Seven Star Weapon that Takt stole, I take it?”
“Indeed. The Claw rightfully belongs to Filo-tan, I say!”
So hand it over to Filo-tan later, Wolf! I glared, but Wolf just stared fixedly at the Claw, ignoring my gaze entirely.
“……This is my brother’s…… Ruhabert Warbult’s chosen Claw Seven Star Weapon, treasure of Siltvelt.”
“Your brother?”
“Yes. I am…… the younger brother who trained alongside him. Magarum…… that’s my name.”
There were still awkward gaps in his speech, but gradually, the one who now called himself Magarum continued, still Wolf in form.

“That man summoned my brother and me to a place with no one around, surrounded us, tore the Claw from my brother, trampled him underfoot, and killed him. I froze in terror at the sight of him mocking us while currying favor with that woman, and I was captured……. After that……”

Bit by bit, the tale of Takt’s misdeeds spilled out. It seemed this one, the younger brother of the Claw Hero, had stumbled upon the very scene where Takt stole the Claw, been captured alive, and afterward had his body and mind twisted as material for human experimentation at Takt’s research facility, losing his memories entirely as a result, before being thrown into the arena in Zeltoble as a gladiator to earn funds.
“I…… back then, I was too afraid to do anything…… but this time, I won’t run.”

Gripping the clawed hand tightly, the one calling himself Magarum stood tall before Father. Then, in a flash, he shifted from his beastman form into his demi-human form. There was something in his appearance faintly reminiscent of the transformed fox-pig Claw Hero that Takt had turned into. His hair was a somewhat tousled short cut, and he appeared to be a muscular man in his late twenties. His whole body was covered in pitiful patchwork-like scars — surely marks left by Takt’s experiments. Come to think of it, after howling and growing a size larger, his coloring had shifted to a deep silver mixed with blue. He truly gave off the air of an experienced, weathered man closer to his thirties, and I found his category quite close to that of Crocodile Guy. That fellow gave a Siltvelt-style salute and bowed his head low.

“I was a beast who had forgotten everything, afraid of everything, but you cared for me with great tenderness — great Shield Hero-sama. This power, this will, I dedicate entirely to Shield Hero-sama. That is my atonement for the brother I lost while trembling and unable to do anything, and my repayment of that debt.”
“I see…… That’s good to hear. So, um, Magarum-san?”

Father is weak against the protective type, so his compatibility with someone like this ought to be good. In that moment, the one calling himself Magarum, upon hearing Father call him by that name, showed a faintly pained expression.

“That name…… is the name I had while trembling in fear. That version of me no longer exists. So, Shield Hero-sama, Naofumi-sama. Please continue calling me Wolf, the name you gave me, just as before.”
“……Yeah. Understood. Let’s keep counting on you from here on too, Wolf.”
“Yes.”

Having answered, Wolf pressed both hands together and bowed deeply to Father, as if swearing eternal loyalty. Hmm…… it felt like, starting from what happened when we went to Siltvelt, the mission to search for the Claw Hero had finally been formally accomplished right here — but for now, the matter at hand was what to do with Takt.
